title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Stream Classes
sourceFile: Stream Classes Basics - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on introduction of stream classes in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which namespace contains the core stream classes in C#?
questions.explanation: The core stream classes, such as Stream, FileStream, and MemoryStream, are defined within the System.IO namespace.

questions.question: Which class serves as the abstract base class for all other stream classes in C#?
questions.explanation: System.IO.Stream is an abstract class that provides a generic view of a sequence of bytes. Since it is abstract, it cannot be instantiated directly.

questions.question: Which method is used to close the current stream and release any resources associated with it?
questions.explanation: The 'void Close()' method closes the stream and releases resources. In modern C#, it is often used alongside the 'using' statement which calls 'Dispose()'.

questions.question: Which method is used to write a single byte to an output stream?

options.text: void Write(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)

questions.explanation: WriteByte(byte) writes a single byte to the current position in the stream and advances the position by one byte.

questions.question: Which method clears all buffers for the stream and causes any buffered data to be written to the underlying physical device?
questions.explanation: The Flush() method moves data from the intermediate software buffer to the physical destination (like a disk).

questions.question: Which is the correct signature for the method used to write a subrange of bytes to a stream in C#?

options.text: void Write(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)
int Write(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)

questions.explanation: In C#, the Stream.Write method returns 'void'. It writes a sequence of 'count' bytes from the provided buffer starting at the specified offset.

questions.question: Which method returns the next available byte of input as an integer, or returns -1 when the end of the stream is reached?
questions.explanation: ReadByte() returns the byte cast to an 'int', or -1 if the end of the stream is encountered.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly define a stream in C#?

options.text: A stream is an abstraction that produces or consumes information
A stream is linked to a physical device by the I/O system
C# programs perform all input and output through streams

questions.explanation: A stream acts as a logical interface to various physical devices (files, network, memory) and handles data transfer sequentially.

questions.question: What is the function of the 'long Seek(long offset, SeekOrigin origin)' method?

options.text: Attempts to read bytes into a buffer
Writes a single byte to an output stream
Sets the current position in the stream relative to a specified origin and returns the new position

questions.explanation: Seek() allows random access to a stream by moving the 'cursor' to a specific position based on the beginning, current position, or end of the stream.

questions.question: Which method attempts to read up to 'count' bytes from a stream into a buffer, returning the number of bytes successfully read?

options.text: int Read(byte[] buffer, int offset, int count)

questions.explanation: The Read method returns the actual number of bytes read into the buffer, which may be less than 'count' if the end of the stream is reached.
